samples.summary: `parseMarginFromEdgeAttr('')` returns 0 instead of the default — a behavioural regression against the backend reader it replaces
samples.evidence: `parseMarginFromEdgeAttr` only defaults when `value === undefined`; for an empty-string attribute `Number('')` is `0`, which is finite, so it returns `0`. The backend code it replaces (`docs-tree.ts`: `attrs.marginFromEdge ? Number(attrs.marginFromEdge) : DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE`) treated `''` as falsy and returned 48. A header/footer node carrying an empty `marginFromEdge` attribute therefore now lays out flush against the page edge instead of at the 48px default. The doc comment claims non-finite/legacy values read as the default, but `''` is neither caught by the writer's `Number.isFinite` filter nor by this reader.

samples.summary: `parseBlockStyleAttrs` accepts an empty-string numeric attribute as 0 (e.g. `lineHeight: 0`), an unrenderable value the guard claims to reject
samples.evidence: `const value = Number(attrs[field]); if (Number.isFinite(value)) partial[field] = value;` — `Number('')` is `0` and finite, so an attribute stored as the empty string yields `lineHeight: 0` / `marginTop: 0` rather than the block default. The backend spec added in this diff even asserts this (`expect(style.marginLeft).toBe(0)` for `marginLeft: ''`), which is benign for a margin but a zero `lineHeight` produces zero-height lines in the layout engine — exactly the class of poisoned legacy attribute the codec was introduced to neutralise.

samples.summary: Omitting non-finite block-style fields on write leaves the stale CRDT attribute in place because `styleByPath` only merges, silently diverging from the in-memory cache
samples.evidence: `applyBlockStyle` does `const attrs = serializeBlockStyle(merged); tree.styleByPath(blockPath, attrs);` and then sets the local cache from `merged`. `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` now omits any field whose value is non-finite (previously it wrote `String(value)`, i.e. `'NaN'`, which the reader turned into the default). Because `styleByPath` merges rather than replaces, a non-finite value (e.g. a NaN produced by a custom line-spacing/indent input) no longer overwrites the previous attribute at all: the CRDT keeps the old value while the local cache/UI shows the new one, and the divergence only surfaces on the next reload or for a remote peer. No corresponding `removeNodeStyle` call exists on this path (contrast the cell-style and inline-style paths, which do pair serialize + remove).

samples.summary: Slide text-body block styles are now value-validated on PUT, but slides data has no read-side normalizer, so a legacy deck can 400 on a GET → edit → PUT the caller never touched
samples.evidence: `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` calls `assertValidBlockStyle`, which rejects any `style.alignment` outside BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS and any non-number/non-finite geometry field (`null`, a numeric string like `"12"`, `NaN`). The docs arm is safe because `parseBlockStyleAttrs` drops those values before the client ever sees them (the comment at line 309 says so explicitly), but the file's own comment at line 570 concedes slide text bodies are "persisted verbatim as JSON (there is no attribute codec to normalize them on read)". Any deck whose stored blocks contain such a value is therefore readable via GET but no longer writable via PUT — the endpoint rejects data it just handed out. The structural requirements were deliberately relaxed for this reason; the value requirements were not.

samples.summary: Group children are now validated as full elements (`id`, `type`, `frame`) — a newly-tightened requirement on verbatim-persisted slide data with no read-side migration
samples.evidence: `assertValidElement(children[i], ...)` recurses with the full element check (non-empty `id`, string `type`, object `frame`) into `data.children`, which was previously unvalidated. Slides elements are stored verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot`, so any nested child that predates one of those fields (or was written by an older importer) makes a previously-accepted PUT return 400. The same recursion is also unbounded, so a deeply nested `group`/`tableData` payload can blow the stack and surface as a 500 rather than a 400.

samples.summary: A table cell with `blocks: []` is accepted by the PUT validator but reads back with a block whose `id` is `''`, which the same validator then rejects — GET → PUT is not idempotent
samples.evidence: The new cell validation only requires `Array.isArray(cell.blocks)` and an object `style`, so `{ blocks: [], style: {} }` (exactly the payload used by the new spec case 'rejects a table cell without a style') is a valid write. `treeNodeToCell` then materialises an empty cell as a block with `id: ''`, and `assertValidBlock` requires `'id' must be a non-empty string`, so a subsequent PUT of the GET result returns 400. Either the writer should reject empty `cell.blocks`, or the reader should synthesise a real block id.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. assertValidBlockStyle (docs-content.controller.ts:314-338) rejects any present style.alignment outside BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS and any present numeric field that is not a finite number (null, "12", JSON-serialized NaN). It is reached for slide text bodies via assertValidElement:533/537/547/553 -> assertValidTextBodyBlocks:578-606. On the read side there is no normalizer: readSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:52-81) returns root.slides verbatim via unwrapJson, writeSlidesRoot:105 stores it verbatim, and the slides migration (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:121-168) migrates layoutId/background/fill/stroke but never block styles. The docs arm is protected by parseBlockStyleAttrs (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts:86-98), whose own comment at :82-84 says it is what keeps the REST GET->PUT identity intact; slides have no equivalent. The controller comment at :567-577 concedes this and relaxed the structural checks for exactly this reason but left the value checks. The spec at docs-content.controller.spec.ts:746-791 asserts 400 for alignment 'middle' and lineHeight null inside slide text/shape bodies, i.e. exactly the values a verbatim-stored legacy deck could return from GET. No guard, caller, or normalizer makes this unreachable, and I cannot rule out existing decks holding such values, so the GET -> edit -> PUT 400 is a real correctness/broken-invariant defect in this lens.

finding.summary: Frontend header/footer `marginFromEdge` read was left without the NaN guard the backend copy just got — a legacy/poisoned attribute still yields NaN in the renderer
finding.evidence: The change hardens the backend reader (`parseMarginFromEdge` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:353 falls back to DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE for any non-finite attribute) and adds a backend test for the literal string `"undefined"`. The frontend store — the code that actually lays out and paints the header — still does `marginFromEdge: Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48')` at lines 526 and 532, so a node written by the pre-guard serializer (`marginFromEdge: "undefined"`) reads back as `NaN`. That NaN flows into `getHeaderYStart`/`getFooterYStart` (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:260,274) and `doc-canvas.ts:272/318`, i.e. NaN geometry in the layout/paint path — exactly the failure mode the backend fix declares unacceptable. The companion writer at lines 728/769/2724/2732 also still does `String(header.marginFromEdge)`, so an absent value is re-persisted as the literal "undefined" instead of being omitted like `serializeMarginFromEdge` now does on the backend.

verdict.reason: The frontend store does not contain the unguarded code described. It uses the same shared codec as the backend: yorkie-doc-store.ts:42-43 imports `serializeMarginFromEdgeAttrs`/`parseMarginFromEdgeAttr` from `@wafflebase/docs` and aliases them at :221-222. Every read goes through the guard (`marginFromEdge: parseMarginFromEdge(attrs.marginFromEdge)` at :492 and :498), and every write goes through `serializeMarginFromEdge(...)` at :694, :735, :2689, :2697. The guard itself (`packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts:121-125`) returns DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE for undefined and for any non-finite value — including the literal string "undefined" — and the serializer (:107-113) returns `{}` rather than persisting "undefined". A repo-wide grep for `String(...marginFromEdge)`/`Number(...marginFromEdge)` yields exactly one hit, inside the guarded serializer at crdt-attrs.ts:111; no unguarded copy exists. The cited lines 526/532 are in `readPageSetup` (`Number(m?.top)`, `Number(m?.right)`), unrelated to marginFromEdge, and lines 728/769/2724/2732 do not contain `String(header.marginFromEdge)`. Because frontend and backend share one module, no NaN can reach getHeaderYStart/getFooterYStart via this path.

finding.summary: New `style.alignment` whitelist on PUT disagrees with the reader, which passes any string through — a read-modify-write (CLI pull/push) of a document holding a legacy alignment value now 400s
finding.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` rejects any `style.alignment` not in {left,center,right,justify}. But `parseBlockStyle` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:177 and the frontend copy at yorkie-doc-store.ts:244) accepts *any* string, including the literal "undefined" that the old unconditional serializer (`alignment: style.alignment` with an undefined value) could have persisted, and any other legacy token. So GET returns `style.alignment: "undefined"` and the very next PUT of that untouched body is rejected with 400 — the round-trip the controller comment calls "identity on the JSON shape" is no longer identity for such documents. The numeric fields were deliberately hardened on the read side (non-finite → default) but `alignment` was not, leaving validator and reader inconsistent.

verdict.reason: The finding's central premise is not present in the code. It claims `parseBlockStyle` "accepts any string" for `style.alignment`, leaving reader and PUT validator inconsistent. In fact both cited locations are mere aliases to one shared codec: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:146` and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:220` both do `const parseBlockStyle = parseBlockStyleAttrs;`. That shared reader, `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts:86-98`, gates alignment at line 91 with `if (isBlockAlignment(attrs.alignment)) partial.alignment = attrs.alignment;` — anything outside the allowlist is dropped and `normalizeBlockStyle` substitutes `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE`. `isBlockAlignment` (crdt-attrs.ts:31-38) is the identical predicate the PUT validator calls at docs-content.controller.ts:321, so the two sides use one allowlist, not two. The specific legacy value the finding names, the literal string "undefined", is covered by an existing regression test: docs-tree.spec.ts:184-208 seeds `alignment: 'undefined'` into the Yorkie Tree and asserts `readDocsRoot` returns `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE.alignment`. Therefore a GET can never hand back an out-of-allowlist alignment, and the described read-modify-write 400 on an untouched body cannot occur. Alignment was hardened on the read side in the same manner as the numeric fields (crdt-attrs.ts:91 vs :92-96), contrary to the finding's claim that it was not.

finding.summary: Block-style validation checks alignment values but still lets `style: {}` through, persisting the literal string "undefined" and NaN geometry into the CRDT
finding.evidence: The new test explicitly asserts `{ blocks: [{ id, type:'paragraph', style: {}, inlines: [] }] }` passes validation. `writeDocsRoot`'s `serializeBlockStyle` then produces `alignment: undefined` and `lineHeight: String(undefined) === 'undefined'` (docs-tree.ts:143-148); `parseBlockStyle` (line 159) does `Number('undefined') → NaN` and `normalizeBlockStyle` spreads that NaN over the default, so `marginTop`/`lineHeight` become NaN and `computeLayout`'s `y += block.style.marginTop` NaNs out the whole document layout. If the controller is now validating block-style *values*, the required numeric fields are the ones that actually corrupt the document when missing.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that `serializeBlockStyle` writes `alignment: undefined` and `String(undefined) === 'undefined'` for absent numeric fields — is false in this repository. `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:145-146` contains no local serializer; it aliases the shared codec `serializeBlockStyleAttrs`/`parseBlockStyleAttrs` imported from `@wafflebase/docs` (docs-tree.ts:28-33). That codec, at `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts:62-74`, guards exactly the case claimed: alignment is written only when `isBlockAlignment(style?.alignment)` (so `undefined` is skipped), and each numeric field does `if (raw === undefined || raw === null) continue;` followed by `if (Number.isFinite(value)) attrs[field] = String(value);` — the literal string "undefined" can never be persisted. The read side is symmetric (`crdt-attrs.ts:86-98`: skips fields not `in attrs`, drops non-finite values) and ends in `normalizeBlockStyle(partial)` = `{ ...DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE, ...style }` (`packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274`), so `style: {}` round-trips to the full defaults, not NaN. The codec's own docblock (crdt-attrs.ts:49-61) names the `style: {}` PUT case as the reason for the guard. Hence `assertValidBlockStyle` deliberately treating every field as optional is correct, and no NaN geometry reaches computeLayout. Ground: already-guarded, one hop away in the shared codec both writers (backend docs-tree.ts and frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts) call.
